html:
The Vasa was a Swedish warship that sank in Stockholm harbour on its first voyage, on 10 August 1628, less than a mile from where it set out.

Built for Gustavus Adolphus during his war with Poland, it was one of the most heavily armed ships of its time, with two gun decks and rich carvings meant to glorify the king. It was too tall and too light below. A gust of wind heeled it over, water poured in through the gun ports, and about thirty people drowned.

The cold, brackish water of the Baltic, free of shipworm, kept the wreck almost whole. It was raised in 1961 and is now shown in the Vasa Museum in Stockholm, the most visited museum in Scandinavia. It shows the ambition of Sweden's great power era. See Sweden.
sum: The Vasa was a Swedish warship that sank in Stockholm harbour on its first voyage, on 10 August 1628, less than a mile from where it set out.
